mechanism.description: US equity closing auctions aggregate time-constrained MOC/LOC and offsetting interest into a deterministic single-price cross. Exchanges publish security-level imbalance, paired quantity and indicative/reference clearing information before the cross. A sufficiently large signed imbalance relative to paired auction liquidity can create temporary price pressure into the close; if the pressure is primarily mechanical rather than information-driven, part of the auction dislocation may normalize after the cross.

non_outcome_public_documentation.fact: Nasdaq disseminates closing-cross NOII from 15:50 to 16:00 ET and documents imbalance, paired and indicative clearing information.
NOII fields and dissemination cadence are formally specified; late closing-window messages are disseminated at one-second frequency.
NYSE documents closing-auction imbalance publication, paired quantity, reference price and the 16:00 ET closing auction.
NYSE provides a real-time feed of buy/sell imbalances during auctions for listed securities.

falsifiable_signal_mapping.signal_clock: Freeze one pre-close observation time before the exchange closing cross; exact timestamp must be preregistered before any economic outcome access.
falsifiable_signal_mapping.signal_direction: signed imbalance direction, conditioned on imbalance magnitude relative to paired auction quantity and contemporaneous indicative-price displacement
falsifiable_signal_mapping.economic_hypothesis: Large mechanical closing-auction pressure relative to available paired liquidity is followed by partial normalization after the auction, opposite the signed pressure direction.

point_in_time_requirements.rule: Only imbalance and reference fields disseminated before the selected closing cross may form the signal. Final auction price, post-close prints and future prices are outcomes and must remain inaccessible until a separately authorized frozen economic test.
point_in_time_requirements.notes: Nasdaq states NOII is subscription data; NYSE historical TAQ imbalance data is a separate historical product. Data entitlement/cost must be qualified before any test.

active_disconfirmation: Imbalances can contain information rather than purely mechanical pressure; continuation rather than reversal is plausible.
Auction participants can offset published imbalances before the close, so early imbalance observations may decay or reverse before execution.
Index rebalance and month/quarter-end sessions may be structurally different and can dominate naive results.
The final auction price is endogenous to the same order flow; using it carelessly as both signal information and execution benchmark can introduce look-ahead or unattainable execution assumptions.
Historical imbalance feeds are proprietary/subscription products; public documentation proves mechanism observability, not free historical data availability.
A cross-sectional signal can be concentrated in illiquid names where spreads, auction collars and impact make apparent normalization non-executable.
The mechanism is not validated by exchange educational material; those sources establish market structure only, not profitability.
